notes.title: Art Book from the game is ready for the premiere
notes.notes:
Do you wonder where visuals from [i]Dr Livingstone, I Presume?[/i] have their roots? Let us introduce the place, where you will find out. Examine each line and each color that marked the final direction. Everything you will see inside the game it comes from right here. [b]The most beautiful concept arts collected on several dozen pages[/b]. Each page arranged with due diligence. Room after room, riddle after riddle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37898672/624debdfddb567f2a4af705b11b61527e43be840.png[/img]

[i]Creating the visual language for "Dr. Livingstone, I Presume?" was as exciting as it was demanding. The key aspect and the first step was to define the boundaries in which I will move in this aspect, the rules that we will have to follow throughout production in order to obtain a coherent vision, and then its implementation. 

Historical background, title hero - David Livingstone and the continent of Africa were the first key starting points here. Another one was low poly style, which we chose for the game. 

So it was necessary to dress the simplicity of the form with something that would break it, make it unique, and this is where hand-painted textures come in. With all this in mind, I expanded these concepts, took inspiration from aspects rooted in the real world. It was clear that we don't seek 1:1 realism here, that we desire to create an audiovisual experience that is unique. 

I wanted the house of David Livingstone (which from the very beginning was supposed to be a "strange house") not only to be an arena we will move around, but also to become a kind of story hero, almost a personage expressing his character, history and emotions that will intertwine with both the narrative and the gameplay to finally offer something, I hope, worth experiencing and remembering.[/i]

~ Paweł Ruszkowski, Main Concept Artist

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37898672/7e1ff5148dca82f4fe14e9decea7a88e72418c0f.png[/img]

You will get it as a gift for the game premiere on May 20, 2021. How do you like it?
